correctness.rationale: For the central right triangle, the sine and cosine rules give sinh(L/2)=s sinh R, tan(theta/2)=cot(a)/cosh R, and tanh r=c tanh R for midpoint distance r and interior angle theta. For a point at distance u from one end of a side, the hyperbolic cosine rule along its incident neighboring side gives cosh d(v)=cosh u cosh v-sinh u sinh v cos(theta). If theta>=pi/2 the unique minimizer is the shared vertex; otherwise tanh v=tanh u cos(theta), yielding an interior foot for u>0 because v<u<=L, and distance asinh(sinh u sin(theta)). The resulting one-neighbor distance is strictly increasing in u. The minimum over both neighbors therefore has a unique maximum at the midpoint. This is the actual maximum over the union of all other sides: at the midpoint a nonneighbor contact candidate has absolute polar angle at least 3a. Match its radial distance on an adjacent side using the same absolute angular offset from that side's midpoint ray, choosing the offset toward the fixed side. The matched absolute angle is at most 2a, so the hyperbolic cosine law gives strictly smaller distance. For n=3 all other sides are neighbors. Thus there are exactly the claimed two nearest points. Independently the Lorentz inner product of the midpoint with an adjacent unit side normal gives sinh of the supporting-line distance as 2s^2 sinh(r) cosh(r)=T, which is the segment distance on the acute branch. On the other branch the segment distance is L/2. The angle crosses pi/2 only for n>=5 at cosh R=cot(a). At the crossing theta'=-tanh R_n and B^2=cos(2a); the first derivatives match, and differentiating B sin(theta) twice versus B contributes -B(theta')^2/sqrt(1+B^2), the stated negative jump. The derivative of T as a function of y=sinh^2 R has positive sign from 1+(2-s^2)y. Expanding T=2c[1+(1/2-1/s^2)/y+O(y^-2)] gives the claimed approach coefficient after applying asinh. The frozen numeric checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The argument concerns fixed n and finite regular convex polygons in curvature -1. Interior feet at R>0 for n=3,4 do not assert a positive transition radius at those n.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Computing the acute formula for a complete line does not resolve the constrained minimization, global midpoint, or finite-radius jump. The ideal formula alone also cannot determine the fixed-n coefficient of convergence. Same-day catalogue dates do not supply ordering or a priority claim.

evidence: Tselekidis defines the same other-side distance condition through segment neighborhoods. The Resultary regular ideal polygon theorem uses complete lines and gives asinh(2 cos(pi/n)) with unique midpoint maximizer.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Polygon thinness in this sense is equivalent to the maximum of point-to-other-sides distances. Replacing finite target segments by full supporting lines is not equivalent: it already gives the wrong compact value in the obtuse branch.

value.rationale: The regular compact family gives an exact benchmark for a standard metric invariant. The endpoint-constrained phase is a genuine geometric feature invisible from ideal polygons or support-line distances; the sharp contact threshold and derivative jump quantify it. The unique midpoint and the exact two-contact classification provide more than plugging a radius into a known limit.
residual_risks: This does not give a general sharp slimness bound for irregular polygons.
